Latin word

cultus

cultus, cultūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a way of life, civilisation: how a people lives, dresses and eats; dress, style of dress, appearance

In this lexicon

  • culture

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1.3: ā cultū atque hūmānitāte prōvinciae longissimē absunt; Cic. de Or. 1.33: ā ferā agrestīque vītā ad hunc hūmānum cultum cīvīlemque dēdūcere

  • style

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 34.4.12: aequātō omnium cultū

  • sine venēnīs cultus, culta, cultum: organic

    * our formation

  • cultus deōrum: religion

    classical

Examples

  • sīc aequātō omnium cultū quid ūnaquaeque vestrum verētur nē in sē cōnspiciātur?

    if all of you dress alike, what is any one of you afraid will be noticed in her?Liv. 34.4.12
